title.tagline: A buyer's diligence brief on a 1986 fixer-upper, 2.4 acres near a tidal creek. The case for, the case against, the all-in monthly cost, and a script for the negotiation. SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE — address, parcel, and MLS are fabricated; every number recomputes from its own inputs.

exec_summary.headline: The Good. The Bad. The Ugly.
good: 2.4 acres, no HOA, no deed restrictions visible — rare in Fairhope's price band.
Roof, septic, and HVAC all replaced 2022–2025; transferable termite bond.
Top-tier schools: J. Larry Newton 9/10, Fairhope Middle 10/10, Fairhope High 9/10.
Built 1986 — no federal lead-paint disclosure trigger.
Tax burden very low: $1,388 in 2025 with homestead.
FEMA Zone X confirmed for the corridor (per neighbor 1013 record).
bad: Listing language explicitly says "fixer-upper" — buyer to verify everything.
Eleven price cuts over ten months: $519,900 → $389,000 (-25%).
Walk Score 0/100 — fully car-dependent rural location.
Septic system, not municipal sewer; well or rural water authority, not city water.
Likely Baldwin EMC for power; no city natural gas; no Fairhope city services.
Property is in unincorporated Baldwin County — Sheriff response, not Fairhope PD.
ugly: Eastern Shore is a "very high" hurricane zone (Augurisk Storm Risk 73%).
April 2014 flood put Fish River 9 ft above base flood elevation.
Two prior listings withdrawn (2014–15 and mid-2025) — possible inspection failures.
Listing status conflict: Active on Zillow, Pending on a third-party feed.
All-in monthly carry at 20% down is ~$2,600 — verify against household budget.
Fairhope median sale up 4% YoY; insurance and tax escalation will compound.

price_history.subtitle: From the initial $519,900 ask to today's $389,000 — 11 reductions and a 25% haircut across two listing cycles. The pattern says either condition is worse than disclosed, prior buyers walked at inspection, or both. Either way, the seller has shown willingness to discount.

climate.title: Climate & Hazard Exposure
climate.subtitle: Storm risk is the headline concern; flood is moderate on a Zone X parcel; wildfire and earthquake are non-issues here. These scores drive what insurance will cost — for a sourced premium range and a quote spec sheet, run property-insurance-brief on this address.

risks.label: STORM (HURRICANE)
risks.body: Augurisk Storm Risk: 73% (severe). 58 named hurricanes since 1930. Sally 2020 caused widespread Eastern Shore damage. Expect 2-5% named-storm deductibles.

risks.label: FLOOD
risks.body: Augurisk: 46% moderate. FEMA Map Service Center confirms Zone X at the parcel. Pull a FIRMette at closing to verify the home pad pad.

risks.label: WILDFIRE
risks.body: Augurisk: 27% low. First Street typically scores Eastern Shore Fire Factor 1-3. Coastal humidity and lawn cover keep risk minimal. Non-issue.

risks.label: RADON (EPA Zone 3)
risks.body: Baldwin is EPA Zone 3 (lowest tier). Average indoor levels under 2 pCi/L. A $50 test kit at inspection covers the diligence.

risks.label: EARTHQUAKE
risks.body: Augurisk: 15% low. Coastal sedimentary plain, not karst limestone. Negligible seismic activity. Non-issue for inspection.

risks.label: LEAD / ASBESTOS
risks.body: Built 1986 — past lead-paint federal disclosure era. Minor asbestos risk in 1980s materials; AHERA inspection only if renovating.

climate.source_note: Sources: Augurisk Fairhope city profile, EPA Radon Zones, First Street Foundation, FEMA MSC.

red_flags.title: What to Resolve Before You Sign

items.title: Severe price-cut pattern
items.body: 11 reductions across two listing cycles and two withdrawals. Either condition issues caused inspection failures or the seller persistently overpriced. Order a top-shelf inspection before proceeding.

items.title: Self-disclosed fixer-upper
items.body: MLS includes "buyer to verify all information during due diligence" language. Repairs may exceed obvious cosmetic scope. Budget for an unknown layer of deferred maintenance.

items.title: Septic system, not municipal sewer
items.body: 2022 upgrade is a positive but you must verify tank size, drainfield condition, Approval-for-Use permit on file, and absence of surfacing or soggy areas. Required: independent septic inspection.

items.title: Hurricane-zone insurance cost
items.body: Augurisk Storm Risk 73%. Eastern Shore is "very high" hurricane risk. Expect $3,500–$6,000+/yr for wind plus homeowners plus flood. Get a binder quote BEFORE removing the financing/inspection contingency.

items.title: Two prior failed listings
items.body: Withdrawn 2014–15 and again mid-2025. Alabama is caveat emptor — the listing agent will not proactively disclose prior deals that fell through at inspection unless you ask. Ask anyway.

items.title: Tax escalation runway
items.body: Property tax up 52% since 2019. Assessment will reset on sale. Plan for $2,800/mo by year 5 even at a fixed 6.30% loan rate. Eastern Shore insurance compounds the bleed.

red_flags.footer_note: These are the items that change the number. Nothing here substitutes for the inspection.

scripts.title: Bring These Into the Negotiation
scripts.subtitle: Three audiences, three lists. Print this slide and take it to the showing, the open house, and the inspection. Do not improvise — work the script.
agent: This listing was withdrawn twice before the current cycle. What happened each time?
Eleven cuts in ten months — did any buyer go under contract and walk? Why?
What specific items led the seller to label this a fixer-upper?
Is the 2022 septic upgrade documented with an Approval-for-Use permit?
Is water private well or East Central Baldwin Water Authority?
Has the seller carried flood insurance? FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area?
Was the 2022 roof installed to Fortified standards? Certificate?
Open or closed code violations on file with Baldwin County?
Any easements, encroachments, or recorded restrictions?
Will the seller provide the CLUE report (5-yr claim history)?
neighbors: How long have you lived here? (gauges institutional memory)
The 2014 area flood — did 1090 take any water?
Hurricane Sally 2020 — what damage did the corridor see?
Road maintenance — county or private? Drainage after heavy rain?
Anyone had well water issues — quality, pressure, supply?
Septic problems on this stretch we should test for?
Any neighborhood issues — noise, drainage disputes, problem properties?
Wildlife and insects on this stretch of river?
inspector: Septic — verify 2022 upgrade, drainfield on a wooded 2.4-acre lot.
Roof — confirm 2022 install, evaluate Fortified retrofit eligibility.
HVAC — pull serial numbers, verify 2022 + 2025 install dates.
Foundation — slab on grade in 1986, look for settling/moisture.
Electrical — 1986 panel may be Federal Pacific or Zinsco (recall items).
Plumbing — check for galvanized supply, polybutylene (1978–96).
Termite — verify transferable bond is current and valid.
Crawl spaces — moisture, vapor barriers, condition.
scripts.footer_note: Print this slide. The questions you don't ask in writing are the issues you find at closing.

phases.title: PRE-OFFER
items: Confirm listing status with the listing brokerage (listing brokerage). Active or contingent?
Pull FEMA FIRMette at msc.fema.gov for the parcel coordinates.
Pull Baldwin County GIS / Parcel Viewer record (parcel 4709310001070).
Run NSOPW.gov sex-offender search at the address.
Request the Alabama property disclosure form.

phases.title: AT OFFER
items: Get insurance binder quotes from at least 2 carriers: wind + HO + flood.
Order title commitment to identify easements, restrictions, liens.
Submit offer at $348K–$364K with 10–14 day inspection contingency.
Request seller to order CLUE report (5–7 yr claim history).
Request seller-paid Fortified Roof inspection for the 2022 roof.

phases.title: INSPECTION
items: Hire 4 specialists per the diligence budget slide.
Add Alabama-required termite / WDO inspection.
Order water-quality test if private well. Independent boundary survey.
Pull permit history from Baldwin County Citizenserve portal.
Pull septic Approval-for-Use from Baldwin County Health.

phases.title: PRE-CLOSING
items: Confirm seller delivers: termite bond transferred, septic permit, well test.
File for new homestead exemption at Revenue Commission within 30 days.
Set up utility transfers: Baldwin EMC, Solid Waste, internet, water.
Final walkthrough day-of-closing.
Allocate $4,725–$8,500 for diligence per inspection budget slide.

offer.title: The Number, The Walk-Away, The Upside
walk_away: Septic inspection reveals failed drainfield ($15K–$30K replacement).
Roof rejects Fortified eligibility AND shows hidden damage.
FEMA confirms Zone AE at the home pad without LOMA available.
reduce_further: Inspection finds more than $25K in deferred maintenance not credited.
CLUE report shows undisclosed wind or water claim.
Boundary survey reveals encroachment or easement issue.
go_to_ask: FEMA confirms full Zone X classification.
Septic in great shape; permit on file.
Foundation clean; electrical updated to current code.
Competing offer materializes (verify, do not assume).
offer.bottom_line: This is a value play, not a turnkey buy. Buy the lot and the schools — pay accordingly for the house.

caveats: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE. Address, parcel ID, and MLS number are fabricated. Do not treat any figure here as real market data.
Monthly carry estimates use the Freddie Mac PMMS rate; your rate will differ by credit profile, lender, and points paid.
Insurance figures are orientation bands, not quotes. property-insurance-brief owns the sourced range and the coverage spec.
Tax projection assumes 6% annual growth; the parcel's trailing 6-yr average was 8%.
Flood zone is parcel-confirmed from the FEMA Map Service Center. Pull a FIRMette before close.
First Street and Augurisk are model outputs, not certainties.
Comp analysis applies typical appraiser adjustments to five recorded sales. property-appraisal owns the defensible value; the appraisal at contract is the only authoritative one.
Alabama is caveat emptor. Buyer's diligence, not seller's disclosure, is the operative protection.
Decision-support only. Not a substitute for a real estate attorney, survey, inspection, insurance binder, or title commitment.
